name: Tameike-Sanno
tagline: Toranomon in 2 minutes and Shibuya in 11 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000.
summary: The station is in Chiyoda City, where Tokyo Metro run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 15 minutes to Otemachi, 14 minutes to Shinjuku, 11 minutes to Shibuya and 16 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. The station stands 9.4 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 19.1 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 9.4 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 6.7 m to 25.8 m, a difference of 19.1 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Even so, 4 of the nine points within 400 m fall inside the area, and the deepest projection there is 0.5 to 3 m. On the whole, the flood projection here is on the small side for the 23 wards.
medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 17 clinics and 21 pharmacies. Day-to-day care is available close to the station. The nearest hospital is 虎の門病院, about 11 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is 友仁会赤坂見附前田病院, about 14 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line run through it. Tokyo Metro Namboku Line also call here. Both lines are run by Tokyo Metro, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: Tokyo Metro Namboku Line runs at 156% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 駒込→本駒込, which this station is not on. Tokyo Metro Ginza Line runs at 153% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch of the line is 赤坂見附→溜池山王, which includes this station. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: Around this station, One room ¥160,000 to ¥170,000 and 1K ¥150,000 to ¥160,000. 1LDK ¥290,000 to ¥300,000 and 2LDK ¥470,000 to ¥480,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.
drivers: Age and construction of the building
Whether it faces a main road or the railway
Whether it sits at the top or the bottom of a slope

rentReason: A one-room flat here goes for ¥160,000 to ¥170,000. Set against how long it takes to reach the central business districts, that is on the high side. What pushes the figure up: plenty of places to eat out. For 1LDK, 2LDK, though, the sources differ by ¥30,000 or more. They count different sets of properties, so read those figures as a range rather than a point.

neighbours.lead: rents are lower at Akasaka, but Tameike-Sanno is ahead on the number of lines.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Tameike-Sanno. Akasaka has only the Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, so Tameike-Sanno is the better connected. To Toranomon, for instance, Akasaka takes 7 minutes longer. A one-room flat, though, costs about ¥12,000 less at Akasaka.

neighbours.lead: Kokkai-Gijidomae is ahead on how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Tameike-Sanno is ahead on how easy the shopping is.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to from Tameike-Sanno. Kokkai-Gijidomae has the Tokyo Metro Marunouchi Line and Tokyo Metro Chiyoda Line, a different set from Tameike-Sanno. To Otemachi, for instance, Kokkai-Gijidomae is 9 minutes quicker. On the number of places to eat out, Tameike-Sanno comes out ahead.

goodFor: People commuting to Otemachi and Marunouchi
notFor: People who want to hold the rent down
noiseSources: The 首都高速都心環状線 viaduct runs just outside the station. It is an expressway, so traffic is audible day and night
The nearest big road, 国道246号, is far enough that little traffic noise reaches the station area

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 9 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 6 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: The station itself is outside the projected flood area, but blocks nearby are inside it.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are on the high side.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is among the highest in the 23 wards.
leads.congestion: Among the 23 wards' stations, the lines here are heavily loaded in the morning.
leads.noiseSources: The big roads are far enough that traffic noise is unlikely to bother you.
